reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) concerns AlxCr1-xCoFeNi alloys with simultaneous Cr reduction, not Al addition to equimolar CoCrFeNi, and reports a minimum friction coefficient of 0.513, which contradicts the predicted ≤0.3. No evidence is provided for Al2O3 glaze formation or low friction across the full RT–800 °C range.
premises: Adding 0.5 at.% Al to CoCrFeNi will form an Al2O3-rich glaze layer during sliding.
This Al2O3 glaze layer will maintain low friction and reduce wear from RT to 800 °C.
The cited AlxCr1-xCoFeNi evidence supports the friction and wear benefits of Al addition.
